findings.summary: Standing /tmp cleanup empowerment is blocked by cross-session file ownership. /tmp/edit-clone (178MB, 22h old) meets all removal criteria (matches /tmp/*-clone glob, mtime > 4h, not the <2h exclusion, not a FUSE mount) but rm -rf fails with 'Permission denied' on every file — the clone was created by another session and its files are owned by nobody:nogroup, not removable by this session's user.
findings.evidence: rm -rf /tmp/edit-clone -> exit 1, 5516 stderr 'Permission denied' lines, e.g. 'rm: cannot remove /tmp/edit-clone/predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json: Permission denied'. stat mtime 2026-06-13 10:26:33 UTC (~22.5h before this run).
findings.impact: Low. Root FS is at 60% used (3.9G free); no actual disk pressure. The 500MB project-footprint trigger is a leak-detection heuristic, not real pressure. The 178MB is recoverable only by the session that owns the clone (or operator).
findings.recommendation: Operator: remove the stale /tmp/edit-clone in a session that owns it, or let its owning session's end-of-run cleanup reclaim it. No agent change needed. If this recurs as a cross-session ownership pattern (stale operator clones that scheduled-agent sessions cannot reap), consider a future PROP to have the operator's clone live under $SESSION/edit-clone (per-session, self-reaping) per the PROP-090 pattern already applied to tinker's own clone.
